Content covers: the transition from the young-bull wood/fire verse (resolved on 27a as referring to the daily lamb-offering) into Rabbi Assi's teaching in Rabbi Yochanan's name that a non-priest who arranges the wood-pile is liable to death, with the practical workaround (the non-priest dismantles it, a priest rearranges it); Rabbi Zeira's challenge asking whether any service is valid at night yet invalid by a non-priest, resolved by distinguishing the burning of overnight fats/limbs (end of the daytime service) and the removal of yesterday's ashes (the start of the daytime service, so a priest already immersed for it need not re-immerse) from the wood-arranging itself; the revised teaching that a non-priest who arranges the two logs specifically is liable (since it is a daytime service), Rava's challenge that this should then require a lottery too, and the baraita resolving that the ash-removal winner also wins the wood-arranging by extension; the question of why the mishnah's list of morning duties omits checking for the two-log time separately, resolved by distinguishing slaughtering's own strict daybreak requirement (with its Levitical verse) from the more flexible logs, whose mis-timed arrangement (if performed too early, by moonlight) has a remedy (dismantle and redo) unlike a mis-timed slaughtering; and the alternate version of Rabbi Zeira's challenge (whether a service followed by another service is invalid by a non-priest to the point of death-liability), continuing onto 28a's fuller citation of the limbs/fats and ash-removal precedents.
